title: Apple Store iPhone Duo Pickup Resumes, But Availability Remains Extremely Limited – MacRumors
body:
Apple has begun re‑enabling its in‑store pickup option for the iPhone 15 Pro models, but the service is still being rolled out on a very limited basis. Customers in several key markets—including Australia, China, Japan and South Korea—can once again add a “store pickup” selection when ordering the iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max through Apple’s online storefront, though inventory remains scarce and the feature is not yet available in many other regions.

The renewed pickup capability marks a partial reversal of the supply‑chain constraints that have plagued Apple’s flagship releases since the device’s launch in September. Early in the rollout, the company temporarily disabled the option in most markets because demand outstripped the limited stock allocated to retail locations. By reopening the system in the four aforementioned countries, Apple appears to be testing whether its logistics network can keep pace with the lingering high demand while also easing the pressure on its online order queues, which have been plagued by long wait times and frequent cancellations.

Analysts see the move as a cautious but strategic step toward normalising the post‑launch sales flow. “Apple’s supply chain has been under unprecedented stress, especially with the ongoing semiconductor shortage and the need to meet a surge of pre‑orders across multiple product lines,” said Priya Desai, a senior technology analyst at MarketPulse. “Re‑introducing store pickup in select markets suggests that Apple has secured enough units to support a limited, controlled distribution, which could help smooth out the back‑log without over‑committing inventory in regions still facing shortages.” The decision also aligns with Apple’s broader retail strategy, which emphasizes a seamless omnichannel experience that blends online convenience with the tactile advantages of physical stores.

The limited rollout underscores the uneven nature of the current inventory landscape. While Apple’s retail outlets in Australia, China, Japan and South Korea are now accepting pickup reservations, many other territories—including the United States and several European nations—still see the feature disabled. In those markets, customers must continue to rely on home delivery, which often involves a waiting period of several weeks or even months for the most sought‑after configurations. This disparity has prompted some consumers to travel across borders or use third‑party resellers, inadvertently fueling a secondary market that inflates prices and complicates Apple’s brand positioning.

From a consumer‑experience perspective, the revival of store pickup could alleviate some of the frustration that has built up around the iPhone 15 Pro series. Shoppers who prefer to collect their devices in person can now avoid the uncertainty of delivery delays and gain immediate access to Apple’s support services, accessories, and warranty registration. Retail staff, meanwhile, are likely to benefit from higher foot traffic and the opportunity to upsell complementary products such as AirPods, Apple Watches, and protective cases. However, the limited stock means that not every reservation will be fulfilled, and Apple has warned that availability will vary by model, color and storage capacity.

Looking ahead, Apple’s next steps will hinge on how quickly it can scale the pickup program beyond the pilot markets. If the limited reintroduction proves successful—delivering a steady flow of devices to stores without triggering stockouts—Apple may expand the service to additional regions in the coming weeks. Such an expansion would signal a broader recovery in the company’s supply chain and could restore confidence among consumers still wary of prolonged wait times. Until then, shoppers eager for the iPhone 15 Pro line will need to monitor Apple’s website closely, act quickly when slots open, and remain prepared for the possibility that the coveted devices may still be in short supply.
